Public views after loss of Wrexham TG Jones and post office

6th October
Business
Leisure
Shopping
Wrexham
By Steve Craddock Court and crime reporter

Share

5 comments
0:00 / 0:00
Read More

Simpler Over Time
Clockwise from top left: Karen Scott, the now empty TG Jones/Post Office unit and Dennis Thomas (Image: Staff)

SHOPPERS and business owners spoke of their disgust and disappointment at losing a vital part of Wrexham city centre's offering.

The Leader reported recently now the city's TG Jones (and the post office within) was to cease trading on September 19.

Now that the unit sits empty, we spoke to people in the city centre about how they feel regarding the closure, the impact it has had and what they would like to see go into the now vacant site.

Karen Scott said: "I am devastated. I always got my electric and gas there and posted my timesheet.

Karen Scott (Image: Staff)

"Now I have to take it and do everything at another post office.

"I did also use the shop too.

"Other people are disgusted too - why are we calling this a city when we don't even have a post office?

"You've got empty shops everywhere too. That's why people say 'oh I go to Chester or Oswestry because there's nothing in Wrexham.'

"It's terrible and [the closure of the post office] is going to affect the Butcher's Market too, because there won't be as many people coming through here."

One man, who didn't wish to be named, said he felt the city centre had lost something important, adding: "It was a good shop."

Steven Vale (Image: Staff)

Steven Vale, Caroline's Viennese Patisserie at Central Arcade, said: "We've lot the post office now - that's another reason for the elderly not to come into town.

"That post office mattered to people."

Mohammed Baez said: "It' really sad, because this is a shopping centre and it has less and less in it - and more empty shops."

Mohammed Baez (Image: Staff)

He added he would like to see another post office back in the unit.

Mandy Roberts said: "That was the only post office around here - it was ideal for the older folks that live in the town. I think it's just s shame."

Asked what she'd like to see occupy the now-empty shop unit, she added: "I don't know, I just hope it's not another vape shop."

Mandy Roberts  (Image: Staff)

Sammy Roberts, who runs the Ride the Wave hand crafted giftware shop in the city centre, said: "I'm surrounded by empty buildings now and it's very disheartening.

"The loss of the post office has had a negative effect on, obviously, sending parcels - because we have online orders too.

"It's more troublesome now, having to go further out of town and it' lugging all the parcels there when we can't get a car up here (due to the bollards).

"I did also use the shop for stationary items - it was great."

Speaking of her views on what Wrexham needs more of, she said: "I think we need more big chains.

"Even though I am an independent retailer, I have always believed they co-habit. They bring people in.

"When people have no reason to come into town, they don't visit shops like mine."

Dennis Thomas  (Image: Staff)

Dennis Thomas told the Leader: "It's awful - I used that shop quite a lot. I think it's disgusting - the town centre's just gone to ruin.

"There's nothing here except bargain shops; nothing decent around. The supermarkets have taken it all, and online shopping."

Habiba Yuzeir said the post office was extremely useful to her where it was, adding: "I don't have a car and I can't take a taxi just to send a letter or to top up my electric or gas.

"The post office was very important."

From left: Chinar and Habiba Yuzeir (Image: Staff)

Chinar Yuzeir agreed, describing the now-closed location as convenient for people in the city centre.

Kerry Jones said: "It's absolutely terrible - we're supposed to be a city now, but even before then - as a town - we need this. Businesses need it, people need it.

"I used it myself and where I work, I speak to people on a daily basis; especially the elderly. It really affects them."

Asked what she'd like to see in the vacant unit, he said: "Obviously we need a post office, I'd like that as soon as possible."

Besides the need for a post office, she said: "It needs to go back to how it was. Years ago, this main street was thriving every day.

Interior of the now empty TG Jones/Post Office unit (Image: Staff)

Signage in the window of TG Jones/Post Office unit (Image: Staff)

  • Teenage Wrexham bookshop owner stunned after Buckingham Palace letter

"We need to bring more of the big name shops we used to have before Eagles Meadow opened; bring them back to the town.

"And butchers - we're crying out for butchers. There's nothing here now - it's all vape shops and tattoo shops.

"That doesn't appeal to a lot of people any more."

A sign placed in the window of Wrexham' empty TG Jones store reads: "We would like to thank you for your custom. Your nearest TG Jones is High Street, Mold."
